title: Scabies therapy with two differently concentrated permethrin creams
official: Phase III multicenter, prospective, randomized, double-blind study comparing the efficacy and safety of therapy for scabies with two differently concentrated permethrin creams.
summary: Main objective: The primary objective of the study is to demonstrate the superiority of the clinical efficacy of the new Permethrin Cream 10% for scabies compared to the standard therapy with Permethrin Cream 5% (primary objective).
criteria:
Inclusion criteria:
1. confirmed acute scabies disease: detection of mites and/or mite nymphs and/or mite larvae, by reflected light microscopy or by light microscopy of skin samples, at predilection sites typical of scabies
2. age between 2 and 85 years
3. written informed consent of the study participant (if of legal age) or from all legal guardians (for study participants under the age of 12) or from all legal guardians and the study participant (for study participants aged 12 or older)
4. feasible application of the trial medication by trained specialist personnel at the trial site
Exclusion criteria:
1. Pre-treatment with antiscabiosa in the last 14 days
2. Planned systemic use of corticosteroids
3. Planned or previous (last 4 weeks) use of systemic or cutaneous non-steroidal immunosuppressants
4. Obvious unreliability or unwillingness to cooperate
5. Inability to understand and comply with study instructions
6. Known alcohol, medication or drug addiction
7. Placement in a facility where people live together for a longer period of time, are cared for or receive medical care, and where close skin-to-skin contact is common (e.g. retirement and nursing homes, facilities for people with disabilities, shelters for the homeless, initial reception facilities/emergency accommodation, hospitals) or placement in an institution ordered by a court/authority
8. 5 or more close contacts (persons with close, extensive skin-to-skin contact with the scabies patient for more than 5-10 minutes)
9. Close contact person who refuses scabies treatment or for whom treatment is not possible (According to the RKI, contact persons of a scabies patient are all persons who have had close, extensive skin-to-skin contact with the patient over a longer period of time (longer than 5-10 minutes), e.g. by sleeping together in the same bed, cuddling, body care and caressing of small children, sexual intercourse, body care of sick persons)
10. Dependence on sponsor or investigator
11. Previous participation in a clinical trial in the last 30 days or in the same clinical trial
12. Combined antiscabious treatment (i.e. simultaneous topical and systemic drug treatment of scabies) in the last 4 weeks
13. Known intolerance to permethrin, other pyrethroids, chrysanthemums or any of the other ingredients of the study medication
14. Scabies crustosa
15. Impetiginization/eczematization requiring inpatient treatment
16. Body weight > 120 kg
17. Pregnancy, breastfeeding
18. Clinically relevant immunodeficiency (of any kind, including extensive local therapy (>20% body surface) with corticosteroids > 2 weeks in the last 4 weeks or ≥ 10 mg prednisolone equivalent >7 days in the last 4 weeks - even without signs of scabies crustosa)
19. Other serious illnesses which, in the opinion of the investigator, prevent the patient from participating in the study
